The Explanation of the Calendar.
THE first column contains the day of the
month, the flood the day of the week, the flood
the festival and other remarkable days; the fourth
the rising and setting of the sun; the fifth the sun's
declination in degrees and minutes, calculated to
the nearest degree in Philadelphia; the sixth the moon's
fouthing; and the seventh the time of sunset
at Philadelphia, computed as the mean between
morning and evening flood, now enough for common use; the morning flood being really twelve
minutes earlier and that of the evening as much
later than the ordinary.
The second column contains an ephemeris of the moon's
place, and the periods when albedo is on the meridian. The time of albedo's passage over the meridian is given for the first six months above the pole, and for the last six below it, five days in each month.
At the days end at midnight, the fouthing of the
moon after that hour is to be fought for against the
following day.
